patient.name: Harold Miller
patient.past_medical_history: COPD, hypertension, former smoker, home oxygen 2 L/min at night.
patient.social_history: Lives with spouse; uses inhalers inconsistently.

timeline.text: ABG confirms acute-on-chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure.

ehr.overview: Older adult with COPD arrives with worsening dyspnea, productive cough, and sleepiness.
ehr.history_physical: Focused exam: tripod position, pursed-lip breathing, accessory muscle use, diffuse wheezes, drowsy but arousable.

notes.note: Client arrives leaning forward, speaking in 2-word phrases, with thick sputum and increasing sleepiness per spouse.
Oxygen started at 2 L/min nasal cannula. Client remains drowsy and wheezing.
After BiPAP and nebulizer, client is more alert and speaks in short sentences.
Client remains on BiPAP, tolerating mask. Work of breathing improved but wheezing persists.

orders.order: Initiate bilevel positive airway pressure per respiratory therapy protocol.
Administer nebulized albuterol-ipratropium now and every 4 hours.
Administer IV methylprednisolone as prescribed.
Titrate oxygen to target SpO2 88% to 92% unless otherwise ordered.
Prepare for intubation if mental status or gas exchange worsens.

diagnostics.result: Hyperinflation; no focal infiltrate.
